producer_report.summary:
The throughput review now measures wasted work. It reports attempts per landed change, money spent on attempts that did not land, and the first-attempt share, over the newest 20 landings and the 20 before them. All of `cargo test -p athena-core`, `-p athena-cli`, `-p athena-data` and `-p xtask` (including the policy scan), clippy and `cargo fmt --check` pass. I did not run the full `cargo test --locked`, and I did not run `cargo run -- status` against the evidence directory.

- **Records:** `ThroughputReview` gains an optional `waste` field and a `wasted` trigger. Old records still parse, and a record with the new field round-trips.
- **Status:** `athena status` prints the three measures with a basis line each. They show even with fewer than 20 landings, with the landing count printed. When a full previous window exists they print beside the newest.
- **Trigger:** a review is also due when attempts per landed change or wasted spend rise more than 20% against the figures the previous review stored. It is also due when the first-attempt share falls more than 20%. From a clean window (nothing wasted before), spend alone does not trigger; attempts per landed change must rise too.
- **Open design request:** it no longer skips the review. The review runs, asks the model, and records the proposal. The note and `THROUGHPUT.md` name the open request.
- **Noise rule for design requests:**
  - A design request is queued only when a measure got worse by more than the larger of the noise between older windows and a one-job floor. Noise is the largest difference between adjacent older 20-landing windows.
  - Under 60 landings noise cannot be estimated, so nothing is queued and the note says "not enough history". The very first review is the exception.
  - A rise within the noise is recorded with `request_job` unset, and the note says it was within noise.
  - Noise from adjacent differences absorbs a steady equal-step worsening. That is documented in `hestia.md` and the CHANGELOG, not fixed.
- **Slowdown request:** it also follows the noise rule when there are 60 or more landings. Below that the existing 25% rule decides, and the note says noise could not be estimated.
- **Docs:** `hestia.md` section 12, the module and function docs in `hestia.rs`, and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated. The old "skips the review" wording is gone.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new status.rs test builds sample records where half of attempts in the window did not land and asserts attempts per landing == 2.0 and first-attempt share == 0.5.
criteria_check.evidence: status.rs test `half_of_the_attempts_not_landing`: 20 landings and 20 failed attempts (40 attempts), 10 landings retry a failed job; asserts window counts (20, 20, 40), attempts_per_landing() == 2.0, first_attempt_share() == 0.5, wasted_usd == 10.0, and the same through Throughput::compute and its text. Also tests for no failures (1.0/1.0/0.0), a 7-landing partial window, an open job, and a closed job that never ran (not counted). `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.

Both pass.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: `slowdown_beyond_noise` takes `(rise, bar, landed)` and returns `Result<Option<String>, String>` (Err = within noise remark, Ok(Some) = noise could not be estimated remark, Ok(None) = beyond) rather than `Result<(), String>`, so the not-estimable remark comes from the same function.

Departure from the plan: `request_gate` takes the four `Measure`s from `Throughput::measures()` plus landed count, first-review flag and open flag, so the pure tests build measures directly; `Measure` and `Bar` are public in status.rs.

Departure from the plan: no `Bars` per-measure `differences` split beyond 1 or 2, and `put_earlier_review_citing`/`earlier_review_with_waste` were folded into one helper `put_review` plus `earlier_review_with_waste`; `seed_failed` takes a slice of landing slots.

The model is asked on every due review, including ones that queue nothing (open question 3 of the plan); under 60 landings no design request is queued after the first review (open question 2); one minute is the median floor (open question 4). These were not put to the user.
display.rs and snapshot.rs are not edited: both print `Throughput::text()` and serialize the struct, so the new lines and fields flow through (listed under unchanged_planned_files).
The steady-trend blind spot (equal-step worsening is within noise) is documented in hestia.md and the CHANGELOG, not fixed.
I did not run `cargo run -- status` against the evidence directory; the status_snapshot test covers the printed text for a one-landing fixture.
mistakes: The first seed_failed fixture set only the invocation's cost, so the records gate refused the commit with 'usage records reconcile'; I fixed it by also setting the per-model cost and recomputing the outcome totals.
My new 'basis' line said 'jobs still open', which made an existing-style assertion on the text 'still open' match THROUGHPUT.md; the test was reworded to look for the open-request sentence instead.
learnings: Invocation cost fixtures must agree in three places: the invocation's `cost`, each `models_used[..].cost_usd`, and the outcome's `totals` (recompute with `crate::scoring::totals`), or the records gate refuses the commit with 'usage records reconcile'.
`RecordId::from_parts(time, bits)` gives deterministic valid ids for test jobs; ids must be YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS plus four Crockford characters.
Floating-point differences such as 21/20 - 20/20 come out a hair above 1/20, so a 'change greater than the one-job floor' test needs an epsilon (NOISE_EPSILON = 1e-9).

status.rs `landed_jobs` (measured only) and the landing count differ: landed jobs that ran no model are landings but have no measured stages, so the median windows and the waste windows are cut separately.
`Throughput` is serialized into the status JSON and the snapshot; the per-attempt cost vector in `WasteWindow` is `#[serde(skip)]` so the JSON gains only the figures.
